questions.prompt: Name a fairy tale or traditional folk tale.
questions.scope: Recognized named traditional folk tales and published literary fairy tales count, including documented fairy-tale novels. Actual translated/alternate titles of a tale share an answer. Whole anthologies, authors and arbitrary modern fantasy novels do not automatically qualify. Different tales are not merged merely because they have a shared ATU plot number or point to a shared character/collection article.
questions.rationale: Two independent whole subjects preserve familiar entry points and source-backed rare answers. Tale title cells, primary collection contents, context-qualified genres and actual written forms are reviewed explicitly. Anthologies, people, bare subjects, source metadata and unsupported labels are held. Shared plot classifications never merge different tales; source rows and subgenres do not create extra prompts.

questions.prompt: Name a literary genre or a form of writing.
questions.scope: Real named story/literary genres, nonfiction and reference forms, and established poem/verse forms count. Qualified subgenres keep their meaningful words. Bare academic subjects, individual book titles, people, physical book parts, musical or film-only categories and unsupported source labels do not automatically qualify.

Tale title cells, primary collection contents, context-qualified genres and actual written forms are reviewed explicitly. Anthologies, people, bare subjects, source metadata and unsupported labels are held. Shared plot classifications never merge different tales; source rows and subgenres do not create extra prompts.
